summary: Heavy steel tower at Big Sandy Lake, erected by 1950; a 1962 report says it was dismantled, but later towermen entries conflict. No source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: A 1962-63 report says the tower was dismantled, while later staffing entries name towermen there. No source says what stands at the site today.

events.note: Canada Lookouts quotes a Department of Natural Resources annual report for 1950-51 recording a new steel tower at Big Sandy Lake in the Northern District.
The same page quotes the 1962-63 annual report: the tower was dismantled and its material removed by helicopter. Later staffing entries conflict.
Local history quoted on the Firetowers site gives Albert Sager as towerman from the late 1960s until his death in 1976.
Towermen list gives Richard Sevigny's years as 1992-2002, with Big Sandy among four towers.

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on whether the tower stood after 1962. The DNR report (quoted on Canada Lookouts) says it was dismantled; the Sager entry (late 1960s to 1976) and the towermen list (Sevigny 1992-2002, Big Sandy among four towers) put staff there later. The story reports both and does not choose. The register's 80 ft heavy steel entry is undated, so it is not tied to the 1950 tower. Brief status, kind and access are unknown and no source settles them, so access is left out. Firelookout.ca and websiteservice coordinates agree. The towermen and register pages are hobbyist compilations that ask for corrections. Searches: one websearch.py query for this tower.
